info.title: OpenAsy SIEM API
info.summary: Security events, Sigma detection rules and the signals they raise.
info.description:
Every screen of siem uses this API, and so can your shippers and scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Send events with `SIEM_INGEST_TOKEN`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description:
One event, or an array of up to 1000. Events are flat JSON objects. If any event in the request is not valid, none of them is kept and the message names the first.

```bash
curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SIEM_INGEST_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"host":"web-1","source":"sshd","message":"Failed password for root"}' \
  https://siem.example.com/api/v1/events
```

The body may be gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), up to 16 MiB unpacked.

Takes SIEM_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

202.description: Kept, and run through every enabled rule.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text in the message or any field.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Events at or after this time.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Events at or before this time.

post.description:
Sigma YAML or JSON. Supported: selections of fields with the modifiers contains, startswith, endswith, re and all; keyword lists; conditions with and, or, not, parentheses, `1 of`, `any of` and `all of` over names, patterns and `them`. A rule with `correlation` instead of `detection` reads other rules by name or id: event_count, value_count (gt, gte or eq), temporal and temporal_ordered, grouped by fields, within a timespan of 1s to 1d. A rule a correlation reads is matched for it even when switched off. Aggregations, timeframes, lt and lte, and correlations of correlations are refused with a message.

Needs the admin role.

Runs rule text over the newest events, so it can be checked before it goes live.

Needs the editor role.

200.description: What the rule would have matched. Nothing is saved or alerted.

patch.description:
Switch it on or off, or replace its text. Signals it made stay.

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
An enabled correlation that reads the rule is changed or deleted first (409).

Needs the admin role.

get.description:
A signal is what one rule found on one host within a window (60 minutes by default): the events are counted, not repeated.

Needs the viewer role.

200.description: Most severe first, then most recent.
The signal with its first events.

patch.description:
A closed or false-positive signal no longer collects matches: the next match is a new signal.

Needs the editor role.

200.description: From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.
Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

post.description:
Returns a one-time enrolment token, valid for 7 days. Start siem-agent with it; the agent then has its own secret (ADR 0023).

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Only an agent that reads no hosts. Its secret stops working.

Needs the admin role.

post.description:
A new one-time token, for an agent that lost its volume. Its old secret stops working; its hosts must trust the new CA.

Needs the admin role.

get.summary: What to put on the hosts this agent reads
get.description:
Its CA public key, the sshd drop-in, the commands to prepare a host (with the systemd-journal group, which reading the system journal needs) and the fixed key.

Needs the viewer role.

post.summary: siem-agent: enrol with a one-time token
post.description: Called by siem-agent, not by people.
Each job is leased for 2 minutes. Answers 409 when the agent's version differs from siem's (ADR 0019).

post.summary: siem-agent: send what a read found
post.description: Secrets in values are masked by the agent, and the events go through siem's rules as POST /api/v1/events does. The cursor moves only once they are kept. Gzip the body.

get.description:
The hosts come from the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052); no route adds or changes one.

Needs the viewer role.

file.description: The hosts file as last read; null without OPENASY_HOSTS.

200.description: The host, read at the agent's next turn.

post.summary: Ask the host for its key again

post.description:
After checking on the host that `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` prints this fingerprint.

Needs the admin role.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when siem runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the siem origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_siem_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when siem is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `SIEM_INGEST_TOKEN`: for log shippers and scripts. It can send events, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

NewEvent.description: A flat JSON object: text, numbers, true/false or null. `time` is an ISO 8601 date or milliseconds since 1970 (default: now); `host`, `source` and `message` are text and are what search and signals use. Up to 64 fields and 16 KiB.

signals.description: Signals created or counted up by these events.

kind.description: detection: matches single events, and makes signals of its own when enabled. correlation: reads the matches of other rules (Sigma correlation) and makes a signal per group when its condition holds.

name.description: Sigma's name of the rule, which a correlation reads it by, as it may by id.

lastError.description: Why the rule was left out or failed, or null.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

limit.description: How many of the newest events to try.

hosts.description: Hosts the matches were on; for a correlation, the groups it fired for.

id.description: Null once the rule is deleted.

incident.description: The incident this signal opened in OpenAsy Incidents, when SIEM_INCIDENTS_TOKEN is set and the signal is at least SIEM_INCIDENTS_MIN_SEVERITY; null otherwise.

state.description: pending: waiting for Incidents, tried again every minute. opened: Incidents has it. failed: given up after a day.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

events.description: The first matching events that are still kept.

open.description: Open signals (new or investigating) by severity.

hours.description: Events in each of the last 24 hours, by the time they happened, oldest first.

start.description: The start of the hour, UTC.

days.description: Signals first seen on each of the last 14 days (UTC), by severity, oldest first.

AgentReport.description: What siem-agent says about itself on every call: its version (it must equal siem's, ADR 0019), its public keys and the host setup.

appliedAt.description: When it was last read and applied; null if it never was.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied.

warnings.description: What to fix that did not stop the file from being applied, such as a host whose agent is not enrolled yet.

HostsFile.description: The hosts file (ADR 0052), shared with Infrastructure. It is read again within a minute of a change; a file that cannot be applied leaves the hosts from its last good version.

fileHostKey.description: The fingerprint hostKey gives in the hosts file: a host that presents that key is trusted without an admin, and no other key can be accepted here.

status.description: Of the last read. new and host-key-pending wait for an admin to accept the host key.

unreadable.description: What the account may not read, such as the system journal without the systemd-journal group, or the audit log.

eventsIn.description: Events read from the host and kept.

keyFile.description: With auth key: a private key in the agent's key folder; the agent's own key without it.

journal.description: journalctl's cursor where the last read stopped; null for a first read, which starts 10 minutes back.

Result.description: One of: events (a read, with where it stopped), hostKeys (the keys a host presents), or error.

more.description: The read stopped at its limit; the host is read again at once.

events.description: Flat events, as POST /api/v1/events takes them. host is set to the host's name from the hosts file, whatever the event says.
